subjective.question: Why studio is an important thing for a broadcasting house? Discuss. (Marks: 3)
subjective.answer: A studio is a primary requirement of a broadcasting house. It is the place from where all transmissions are made and programs are recorded in a very orderly manner. What makes a studio different from an ordinary room is the special treatment given to its walls, which are covered with a variety of substances to ensure that no sound passes through them — that is why they are called sound-proof. Special leather covering or carpet is put on the floor so that no sound is produced even if someone walks inside, and the doors are so tightly closed that any sound produced outside is not heard inside. Studios are fitted with proper microphones, recording systems, lights and booths for producers to control recordings or transmissions. Different forms of studios — news studio, studios for talk shows and discussions, drama studio and music studios — serve different programs, so without a proper studio, quality recording and live transmission are not possible.

subjective.question: What are the important points that should be kept in mind while writing script for radio documentary? (Marks: 3)
subjective.answer: The important points are: (1) All facts and figures about the subject must be checked and verified, for a documentary is placed in archives and kept as a future reference. (2) The producer must use imagination in giving treatment to the subject, but objectivity must not be over-shadowed by subjectivity, otherwise the documentary loses its essence. (3) The script should be punctuated with insertions — brief pieces of interviews of relevant people and experts, inter-cut at appropriate points instead of long talks at one go. (4) The producer should visit the actual place to get a real feel of the surroundings, instead of making the documentary sitting inside a studio. (5) The narration should be written in a way that creates and holds the interest of the listeners. (6) Careful post-production must be planned, as flaws in recording are removed at that stage.

subjective.question: Write about any 2 types of documentaries. (Marks: 3)
subjective.answer: (1) Narrative documentary: Here a talent describes the subject matter with facts and figures and articulates the narration so as to create interest about the topic. For example, in a documentary about the Texila ruins, listeners are told when the Texila civilization came into existence, how the people lived there, what artifacts have been recovered and what language those people used to speak. (2) Musical documentary: This type explains the topic in a script frequently punctuated with musical insertions. It is done when a documentary is required on a personality closely linked with music, or on birds, rivers, nature and tourism, where voice superimposed on musical notes enhances the value of the script.

subjective.question: How semantics create barriers in the smooth communication process? (Marks: 5)
subjective.answer: Semantics is the study of meanings of words. Semantics creates barriers because the same word or message does not carry the same meaning for every person. Meanings depend on the psyche, background, education, culture and social status of the sender and the receiver. As discussed in the course, a message from rich to poor and the same message from rich to rich will carry a different meaning — for instance, a chairperson asking another chairperson to attend a marriage party, and the same message conveyed to low ranking staff, carries a different psychological approach. Words having more than one meaning, difficult words and jargon are decoded by the receiver according to his own understanding, not according to the intention of the sender. In this way the true meaning of the message is distorted and the smooth communication process is hampered. The remedy is to use simple and commonly understood words, keeping the audience in view.

subjective.question: Modern advertiser is like a business and he does not sponsor purposeful and cause oriented programs or broadcast. To what extent do you agree with it. Explain about it. (Marks: 5)
subjective.answer: To a large extent this is true. Advertising is a commercial activity, and the modern advertiser behaves like a businessman who invests money only where a return is expected. Studies are regularly conducted by advertising agencies to find out which programs are liked by the target groups, and advertisers prefer entertainment programs — musical programs, sports or humorous programs — because these are listened to by more people and the response is usually good. Sponsorship of whole series, matches and dramas is also done for commercial benefit. Purposeful and cause oriented programs do not promise a large audience or direct sales, so advertisers generally do not sponsor them. However, broadcasting houses themselves do produce purposeful programs as part of their service to society, and some advertisers do support such programs for goodwill. But by and large, the modern advertiser sponsors programs for business reasons, not for a cause.

subjective.question: Discuss the personality feature with an example. (Marks: 2)
subjective.answer: A personality feature is a radio feature which gives a detailed view of a person — his life achievements, living style and contribution to the sphere of his profession. For example, Dec 25 is approaching and the broadcasting house is mindful to produce a feature on Quaid-e-Azam. A team is set up much before that day; the feature comprises a complete profile of Quaid's life, his thoughts, struggle, campaigns, political odds he faced, parleys he held with the Raj and Congress, his leadership qualities, research done by various scholars and references of books and articles written on him, with a conclusion which is relevant today.

subjective.question: What are the globally defined audience patterns that are always considered by the advertising agencies while preparing a publicity campaign? (Marks: 3)
subjective.answer: The segments of people have been globally identified as follows: men, women (in general), children up to 13 years, youth 14 to 30, middle ages 31 to 50, middle ages but in low income group, people in upper income group — and in another way, typical rural listeners and typical urban listeners. No advertisement agency can ignore these well defined segments of audience while preparing a publicity campaign on radio or TV.

subjective.question: There was once a typical heavy looking microphone but now they are so many in types and shapes. Enlist any six types of microphones. (Marks: 3)
subjective.answer: The six types of microphones are: (1) Broadcast type, (2) Outdoor recording, (3) In-built in various voice recording and actuating devices, (4) Small stick with headphones, (5) Collar mikes, (6) Mobile phone mikes. Some microphones are also fitted with wind-screens which block air (breathing) interference with voice.

subjective.question: Explain with the help of an example that stress on the word changes the meaning of the speech. (Marks: 5)
subjective.answer: Stress on a word, or a syllable, changes the meaning of the speech. Take the sentence: 'Nadeem will go to Islamabad next week.' If we stress NADEEM, it means Nadeem (and not someone else) will go. If we stress ISLAMABAD, it means he will go to Islamabad (and not to some other city). If we stress NEXT, it means he will go next week (not this week), and if we stress WEEK, it means the period is a week (not a month). Thus, by changing the stress on different words of the same sentence, every time we are likely to get a different meaning.

subjective.question: Briefly explain the link between broadcasting house and transmitter. (Marks: 5)
subjective.answer: This is a much explained topic, the link between broadcasting house and transmitter. Transmitter plays a role of bridge for connecting listeners and broadcasting houses. Transmitter is a big electronic device, which receives the signals through the electric waves. We can say the link between broadcasting house and transmitter is like the back bone of a system, which can't run without it. If transmitter goes down or there is some technical problem occurred with it, it can be the cause of disturbance for the listeners. The transmitter is the one and only connecting source with broadcasting houses: the broadcasting house sends ready-for-broadcast signals to the transmitter through ordinary transmission lines, or microwaves, and the transmitter broadcasts them at the allotted frequency for the end listeners.

subjective.question: How medium itself can be a barrier in communication process? Briefly discuss. (Marks: 3)
subjective.answer: The medium used for communication can itself become a barrier when it is weak, low quality or under the influence of other factors. For example, in broadcast transmission, amplitude modulation (AM) faces the problem of static current produced by thundering clouds, a motorbike with a damaged spark plug, or high tension overhead wires. The distortion so created does not allow a listener to hear what is being broadcast, and the true meaning of the message is hampered. In this way the medium itself, instead of carrying the message smoothly, becomes a source of noise in the communication process.

subjective.question: How do you look at the future of DJs in Pakistan? (Marks: 3)
subjective.answer: The future of DJs in Pakistan is bright. With the arrival of FM stations, radio listening has grown a great deal mainly because much of the FM transmission is based on lively, interactive programs, and disc jockey programs fill the long hours of transmission in an entertaining way. Film and album songs with a touch of pop and rock are the hot favorites for the disc jockeys. However, performing as a DJ is not an ordinary job: the talent must be trained enough to understand the exact requirement of the job, the script must be practiced regularly and all properties of speech should be exploited to keep the interest of the listeners intact. With more FM stations, internet radio and podcasting growing in Pakistan, trained DJs with good talk and presentation skills will have increasing opportunities.

subjective.question: Discuss the five different manners in which insertion orders can be made on Radio or TV channels as per request of the advertising agencies. (Marks: 5)
subjective.answer: An insertion order, also called release order, is sent by an advertisement agency to a radio station, magazine or TV channel, requesting the ad to appear in any of the following five manners: (1) Integrated — as if part of an interesting program, causing no irritation to listeners; for instance, a particular ad appearing in all dramas of a series. (2) Non integrated — inserted in-between programs. (3) Trailer — a brief commercial, with detailed ads later in a program. (4) Spot — marking the time when the ads should appear. (5) Time signal — first gives the time, followed by a brief announcement.

subjective.question: What are some of the FM station Services? Discuss.
subjective.answer: FM station services are of many types, and FM radio has a huge amount of listenership. Its main services are: Entertainment — a house wife can enjoy the radio station services during the tough routine, children can also enjoy their Sundays in children programs, young people after leaving their jobs can relax their mind during the evening drive shows, and the radio services satisfy old aged people in their loneliness. Marketing — FM is the best platform for commercialization; people can easily get information about new trends and sellers also get benefit from FM station services. Awareness — a huge number of people listen to radio, so radio station services are the best for moral inner development; some RJs and DJs facilitate the people, giving them morality and a vision of life. In addition, as a regular feature a number of FM stations provide useful announcements for listeners, especially those who are traveling — weather reports after regular intervals, currency exchange rates, PIA flights and train timings.

subjective.question: Why classification is needed in radio dramas?
subjective.answer: Classification is needed in radio dramas because it was realized that every drama did not attract everyone. When the audience analysis approach was introduced and listeners were categorized on the basis of research, it became clear that different segments of listeners have different interests. So there were separate dramas for children, military personnel, farmers and rural people, urban aristocratic class and one for the general public. In another way radio dramas were classified as historical, translations, romantic (the most listened category), war-time, and on social life, mainly showing bad characters getting defeated. This classification helps the producers to make dramas according to the taste of the target audience.

subjective.question: For folk singers Radio Pakistan turned out to be a great blessing. Discuss.
subjective.answer: Yes, it is the biggest achievement of Radio Pakistan that there are so many folk singers who were blessed with spiritual folk voice and they started singing from this platform of Radio Pakistan. During the war of 1965, Madam Noor Jahan played a very important role for the motivation of the nation from the platform of Radio Pakistan. Folk singers' voices gave them a big name and they were a cause of the goodwill of Radio Pakistan. There are so many folk singers of Radio Pakistan who got national and international awards. At that time, Radio Pakistan was famous all over the world because of these voices. Pathane Khan was a very blessed folk singer, who started singing from the platform of Radio Pakistan. It was the time when folk singers sung on the demand of the listeners; there was great demand for folk music on Radio Pakistan. There are also famous names of Radio Pakistan like Abida Parveen, Saeen Zahoor etc. So Radio Pakistan was a great blessing for beautiful, inspirational and motivational folk voices.

subjective.question: What is a curtain raiser? Discuss its purposes with examples.
subjective.answer: A curtain raiser is a full program in itself which is broadcast before an event or activity to throw light on a topic and to place listeners in a position where they would be able to understand all the aspects of the coming event. A curtain raiser is meant to cover all possible aspects of the event. It is prepared for events like meetings and visits of important personalities (political), sporting events like a series of test matches (sports), academic activities like conferences and foreign universities holding camps for students (academics), and other stray events like the inauguration of a port.

subjective.question: Define noise. Discuss the different forms of physical noise in the communication process.
subjective.answer: In communication, noise means anything in any form, which distorts or hampers the true meaning of a message. Physical noise has the following forms: (A) Medium itself — the medium used is weak, low quality or under the influence of other factors, just as the amplitude modulation problem in broadcast transmission when static current is produced by thundering clouds, a motorbike with a damaged spark plug or due to high tension overhead wires. (B) Problem at sender's end — for example, you are making a telephonic call and there is so much sound around you, it may be a railway platform; you may be asking someone to pick you at three but due to rustle around you, the receiver understands three as free. (C) Problem at receiver's end — the receiver is at a place which is very hurly-burly and full of clamor, and may not understand the message; in such a situation the receiver rushes away to find a calm place so that the message could be understood.

subjective.question: What is pod-casting? How can a person start his/her own radio station on the net?
subjective.answer: Pod-casting is creating your own radio station on the net with almost negligible cost on software and little arrangement on what you intend to broadcast. No license taxes or checks are applicable so far. To start it, you only need to possess ample knowledge of RSS (Really Simple Syndication) files, which is a format that helps in making programs which you could allow your subscribers and friends to access on your website. An added knowledge of MP3 format is a great help also. These two types of audio files do the whole business for you to run a broadcasting facility on the Net.

subjective.question: Differentiate between AM and FM transmission.
subjective.answer: In the case of Amplitude Modulation (AM), the sound waves, after being put along the electromagnetic waves, are given treatment only to the amplitude of the wave, and not to its frequency. In the case of Frequency Modulation (FM), the number of times the wave spins (its frequency) is increased instead of its height, or amplitude, being disturbed. AM has been strong and could be transmitted to more distance as compared to FM, but the problem with AM is that it interacts more with static charges, like those coming from thundering clouds or the waves emitting from a spark plug of a motorbike, so the quality of transmission has to be compromised. On the contrary, FM transmission is less prone to interferences caused by static charges or electrical sparks and takes the original broadcast strongly to the end point of its range, which is fairly less than AM because FM transmission is based on the physics principle of line of sight.
